paper.title_en: Constraints on the Physical Association between ICECAT1 Neutrinos and Fast Radio Bursts Using the Second CHIME/FRB Catalogue
paper.abstract_en: We present a search for neutrino counterparts to fast radio bursts (FRBs) using temporal and spatial cross-matching between the 1423 non-repeating FRBs of the Second CHIME/FRB catalogue and the 73 alerts of the IceCube high-energy alert-track catalogue ICECAT1 from 2018 July 25 to 2020 December 31. Because current FRB-neutrino models do not agree on the emission order, we adopt a two-sided temporal hypothesis and define the significance criterion from the expected number of chance coincidences before the search. We find no statistically significant association: no pair lies within the $3σ$ and $5σ$ coincidence windows of $3.50 \times 10^2$ s and $7.43 \times 10^{-2}$ s, and the pair closest in time, FRB20190630C-IC190629A, is consistent with a chance coincidence ($p = 0.254$, $0.66σ$). Using a population-level stacking analysis, we derive 90% upper limits on the neutrino-to-radio luminosity ratio of FRBs, $ξ\lesssim 1.4 \times 10^{11}$ for a neutrino spectral index $γ=1.0$ to $6.8 \times 10^{12}$ for $γ=3.0$, assuming neutrino emission within the burst duration. For a neutrino number spectrum $dN/dε\propto ε^{-2}$, the corresponding limit on the neutrino fluence per burst is about a factor of 4 below those of previous stacking searches. For $γ=2$, the limits on the isotropic neutrino energy, $10^{49}$-$10^{52}$ erg, lie more than five orders of magnitude above the predictions of magnetar-driven shock models, so the present data do not constrain these models. Nevertheless, our blind significance criterion and population-stacking limits provide a baseline for future multi-messenger searches.
